facts.text: The user wants to generate a knowledge graph from an FAQ about KrisFlyer “Pay with Miles/Mix Miles and Cash”.
The FAQ describes a project called “Pay with Miles” (PwM) / Mix Miles with Cash for KrisFlyer (KF) members.
The FAQ states that KF members can use KF miles as payment or partial payment of commercial tickets and selected ancillaries on singaporeair.com (SAA).
The FAQ states that KF members can use this payment option for all commercial booking classes available on SAA.
The FAQ states that KF members can control the number of miles used as long as it is more than the minimum required.
The FAQ states that a minimum of approximately 1050 KF miles is required per transaction (per PNR).
The FAQ states that the minimum miles requirement may vary because the conversion rate from SGD to KF miles is subject to change.
The FAQ states that the conversion rate is stored as SGD 1: 105 KF miles.
The FAQ states that the KF miles deducted for such a transaction will always be in multiples of 105 miles.
The FAQ states that there is no maximum number of miles allowed to be used.
The FAQ states that members can pay up to 100% of the commercial ticket using miles, inclusive of airport taxes and surcharges.
The FAQ states that purchase of miles is not available for this payment method.
The FAQ states that purchase of miles is only available when redeeming award tickets or flight upgrades.
The FAQ states that members can use miles to pay for airport taxes and surcharges on commercial tickets bought on SAA.
The FAQ states that the entire commercial ticket can be paid for with miles.
The FAQ states that members can use miles to pay for the commercial tickets of their nominees (RGN) only.
The FAQ states that members can nominate up to a maximum of 5 RGNs.
The FAQ states that nominees can be added at any time.
The FAQ states that once added, RGNs cannot be removed or changed for a period of 6 months.
The FAQ states that a fee is applicable for changing nominees within the stated constraints.
The FAQ states that members can only use their miles for SIA operated flights.
The FAQ states that if an itinerary on SAA includes a codeshare flight operated by another airline, KF miles cannot be used to pay for the SIA operated flight within that itinerary.
The FAQ states that KF miles payment option is only available for KF members via SAA.
The FAQ states that KF miles payment option is not available for bookings made through a travel agent.
The FAQ states that itineraries originating from outside Singapore are priced in local currencies and converted to SGD based on IATA rounding logic before being converted to KF miles.
The FAQ states that the current SGD to miles conversion rate is SGD 1 per 105 KF miles.
The FAQ states that the conversion rate will be reviewed periodically and is subject to change.
The FAQ states that the conversion rate is not explicitly made known to members on SAA content pages and booking flow.
The FAQ states that if members enquire about the conversion rate or monetary value of miles, the conversion rate can be shared as SGD 1 per 105 KF miles.
The FAQ states that KrisFlyer and Elite miles will be earned in proportion to the fare excluding airport taxes paid using credit/debit card if the fare is mileage accruable.
The FAQ states that PPS Value accrued is derived from the proportion paid using credit/debit card.
The FAQ states that the current conditions for accruing and calculating PPS Value still apply.
The FAQ states that KF miles used to pay for a transaction first offset all airport taxes of all tickets before being used to offset fare and fuel surcharges.
The FAQ states that Elite miles and KF miles accrued on tickets partially paid for using KF miles can only be accrued to the KF account.
The FAQ states that miles accrued on such tickets cannot be parked with any other OFFPs.
The FAQ states that members cannot opt to accrue miles for other KF members before themselves.
The FAQ states that accrual logic is optimized to benefit the principal member and members cannot adjust this logic.
The FAQ states that miles earned from a commercial ticket paid for with KF miles can only be credited to the member’s KF account.
The FAQ states that commercial tickets paid for with KF miles are strictly non-endorsable.
The FAQ states that redemption upgrades are allowed for tickets paid for with KF miles if the commercial fare is in an upgradeable booking class.
The FAQ states that for flight or itinerary changes, members must contact their local SIA office or call centres.
The FAQ states that any additional collection resulting from changes can only be paid using credit card, debit card, or cash.
The FAQ states that fare conditions apply to changes.
The FAQ states that members can submit booking change requests via SAA which are routed offline for handling.
The FAQ states that seat and meal requests can be self-serviced on SAA.
The FAQ states that offline assistance for issuing a ticket paid for with miles by AROs/call centres is for exceptional handling only.
The FAQ states that the payment feature is only available on SAA.
The FAQ states that if SAA is down, KF miles will not be an available payment option at that time.
The FAQ states that members can continue to complete the transaction offline if SAA is down, but payment must be made using credit/debit card.
The FAQ states that members can make seat and meal requests on SAA after bookings are reissued offline by AROs/call centres.
The FAQ states that tickets paid for with KF miles can be submitted for refunds on SAA if the tickets are completely unflown and have not been reissued.
The FAQ states that for refunds, the maximum amount paid using credit/debit card will be refunded first, not exceeding the original amount paid using credit/debit card.
The FAQ states that the balance refund is then refunded in miles.
The FAQ states that KF miles that have expired will not be refunded.
The FAQ states that refund logic for cancellations refunds the cash amount first (not exceeding the original amount paid using credit/debit card) before refunding KF miles.
The FAQ states that residual value refund when reissuing from a higher fare to a lower fare follows the same cash-first then miles logic.
The FAQ states that for booking changes from higher fare to lower fare, the cash amount is refunded first and any balance is refunded in miles.
The FAQ states that expired KF miles will not be refunded in these refund scenarios.
The FAQ states that expired miles used to pay for the flight are not refunded.
The FAQ states that only miles that have not expired can be refunded.
The FAQ states that applicable fees and charges associated with the refund are deducted from the oldest miles used for the ticket.
The FAQ states that expired miles will be used to deduct such charges first.
The FAQ states that expiry information for miles used for tickets is available in the transaction record in MARMS.
The FAQ states that after the refund mask is created in Altea, expiry information is displayed as a response from MARMS.
The FAQ states that members are advised of this expiry information if they submit tickets for refund on SAA.
The FAQ states that members can submit tickets paid for with miles for refund on SAA or by contacting their nearest SIA office.
The FAQ states that for tickets submitted for refund offline, the tickets must be refunded by the original issue station.
The FAQ states that miles are returned to members’ accounts immediately once the refund is successfully completed.
The FAQ states that the new payment option is only available on SAA for new ticket issuance.
The FAQ states that KF miles are only available as a payment method for commercial tickets.
The FAQ states that the list of SIA services members can use KF miles to pay for is being increased.
The FAQ states that members cannot use miles to pay for taxes and surcharges on redemption award tickets.
The FAQ states that enabling members to pay for taxes and surcharges on redemption tickets is planned for the next phase of development.
The FAQ states that enabling members to use miles to pay for taxes and surcharges on redemption tickets and other SIA services is planned for the next phase of development.
The FAQ states that OFFP members (e.g., LH Miles & More member using LH miles) cannot use their own miles if they are not KrisFlyer members.
The FAQ states that only KF miles can be used for this new payment option.
The FAQ states that only KF members who accrue KF miles can use this payment option.
The FAQ states that members can continue to redeem Saver, Standard, and Full Award tickets using KF miles.
The FAQ states that the payment feature is an additional programme feature that increases the number of options for members to use their miles.
The FAQ states that the number of miles required to pay for a commercial ticket depends on fares available at the time of purchase.
The FAQ states that members are advised to check mileage requirements for both commercial tickets and award redemption and consider applicable fare conditions.
The FAQ states that infant nominees are not available in the dropdown list on SAA currently.
The FAQ states that once infant nominee feature is made available on the commercial booking flow, members will be able to pay for infant tickets with miles.
The FAQ states that members can book for themselves and/or nominees and other passengers who are not nominees.
The FAQ states that members can only use miles to pay for tickets for themselves and their nominees.
The FAQ states that members must pay for tickets of other passengers not covered by miles using credit/debit card.
The FAQ states that for itineraries starting from MI destinations, MI cannot service reissue/revalidate/refund for tickets paid for with miles.
The FAQ states that tickets involving collection of miles must be routed to SQ for handling.
The FAQ states that this routing is similar to handling of redemption tickets.
The FAQ states that when voiding a reissue of a ticket originally paid for with miles, the FOP for the reissue must be deleted before attempting another reissue.
The FAQ states that MARMs returns an approval code for all reissue tickets and the approval code is appended into the FOP field.
The FAQ states that when the reissue ticket is voided, a void message is sent to MARMs and the approval code is invalidated by MARMs.
The FAQ states that if the FOP is not deleted, Altea will use the same approval code to issue the new ticket and the new ticket number will not be updated by MARMs.
The FAQ states that subsequent servicing such as reissue or refund will fail because MARMs has no record of the new ticket.
The FAQ states that voiding the refund of a ticket originally paid for with miles is not allowed even when the sales report is not closed yet.
The FAQ states that Altea does not send any void message to MARMs for voiding of a refund record for tickets originally paid with miles.
The FAQ states that because MARMs is not aware the refund is voided, subsequent attempts to refund the ET will fail.
The FAQ states that for tickets paid for with miles, refund must be refunded by the original issue station.
The FAQ states that if refund is done by a different station, BBR is used to convert refundable amount to the refund station currency.
The FAQ states that MARMs only stores IATA exchange rate.
The FAQ states that the BBR-converted amount may be higher than the MARMs-converted rate, resulting in refund failure.
The FAQ states that cover refund is permitted for a flown ticket but not for an already refunded ticket when tickets are paid for with miles.
The FAQ states that Altea calls MARMs for all refunds of tickets paid for with miles.
The FAQ states that MARMs has a record that the ticket is already refunded, so further refund is not allowed.
The FAQ states that MARMs has no record that the ticket is flown, so cover refund is still allowed for a flown ticket.
The FAQ states that zero refund is not allowed for tickets paid for with miles.
The FAQ states that MARMs expects to receive FOP details for tickets paid for with miles in the refund message from Altea.
The FAQ states that there is no FOP for zero refund, so zero refund is not allowed for tickets paid with miles.
The FAQ states that for reissue of tickets paid for with miles, only cash is allowed if additional fare is required.
The FAQ states that FQTR is mandatory for such reissues and also for reissue without adc.
The FAQ states that MARMs needs the FQTR number from Altea to create the MARMs record for the reissue transaction.
The FAQ states that if a member wants to use 100% of the miles for their own ticket only, they can select “Not a nominee” and manually type in the 2nd pax details.
The FAQ states that accrual logic defaults to always favour the principal member.
The FAQ states that the principal member accrues full miles before the nominee (also a KF member) accrues any miles.
The FAQ states that if the principal member chooses “Not a nominee” and enters the 2nd pax details manually, the principal member cannot use miles for the 2nd pax.
The FAQ states that in this case, the principal member gets either partial or no accrual while pax 2 gets full accrual.
The FAQ states that a residual value eMD issued against a ticket paid for with miles cannot be reissued into another ET or eMD.
The FAQ states that such reissue is not in scope for phase 1 and MARMs returns an error message to Altea causing reissue to fail.
The FAQ states that the eMD must be submitted for refund and this will be reviewed by LMD in phase 2.

keyphrases: SGD to KF miles conversion rate
refund logic cash first then miles

events.text: Nominees cannot be removed or changed for a period of 6 months after being added.
Refund of tickets paid for with miles returns miles immediately once the refund is successfully completed.
Residual value eMD reissue is not in scope for phase 1 and will be reviewed by LMD in phase 2.
Enabling miles to pay for taxes and surcharges on redemption tickets and other SIA services is planned for the next phase of development.
